patch_description: Instead of routing each destination independently with Dijkstra (which re-sends data over shared edges once per destination), this approach treats the broadcast as a directed Steiner tree problem: it computes a union subgraph of low-cost paths from src to all destinations, then repeatedly contracts shared edges so that the source's data only needs to be transferred once along shared trunk links. For each destination, we run Dijkstra on a "shared-cost" metric where an edge already carrying data to another destination is discounted (cost multiplied by a small factor), encouraging paths to reuse existing trunk edges. This reduces redundant transfers across common cloud backbone links and directly lowers total data transfer cost. All partitions for a destination follow the same shared tree path, keeping the structure simple and robust (Dijkstra fallback guarantees no failures).
